stages.about: What philosophy and awakening are, Socrates as the model and Hellenism as a living path: the ground every later stage stands on.
The soul and its parts, nous and the senses, being and becoming, forgetting and recollection: who it is that makes the journey.
Living well, virtue, justice, freedom, paideia and the polis: how the soul lives with itself and with others before the ascent begins.
Eros as a path, Diotima's ladder to Beauty, and love as unity: the force that draws the soul upward once the good life has steadied it.
Apollo, the oracle within, and his powers of healing, mantic knowing, aim and music: the steps of awakening that lead out of the cave.
The allegory itself, its shadows and their makers, the turn, the Sun and the Good: read with the soul, virtue, eros and Apollo's steps already known.
Heraclitus' fire and Logos, the One, Plotinus and non-duality, Pythagoras' number and the turning of time: the cosmos seen from outside the cave.
Myth as symbol, the gods as powers of the soul, dying before death and the second birth: the initiatory meaning of the stories, read with all that came before.
The Odyssey and nostos, immanence, Hellenic meditation and daily practice: coming home, and living the One in ordinary life.

call.about_en: Philosophy as Athena teaches it: a lived path and an eros for truth, whose aim is to touch it.
call.about_el: Η φιλοσοφία όπως τη διδάσκει η Αθηνά: ένας βιωμένος δρόμος, ένας έρωτας για την αλήθεια, με σκοπό να την αγγίξεις.

call.about_en: Socrates’ not-knowing and midwifery of souls, Plato who carried them on, and the Delphic “know thyself”.
call.about_el: Η σωκρατική απορία και η μαιευτική των ψυχών, ο Πλάτων που τις συνέχισε, και το δελφικό «γνῶθι σαυτόν».

call.about_en: What awakening is and is not, how lukewarm spirituality disarms it, and how pain and crisis wake us.
call.about_el: Τι είναι και τι δεν είναι η αφύπνιση, πώς την αφοπλίζει η χλιαρή πνευματικότητα, και πώς μας ξυπνούν ο πόνος και η κρίση.

call.about_en: Hellenism as a universal spirit, what makes a Hellene, the Greek language, and the golden thread of teachers.
call.about_el: Ο ελληνισμός ως οικουμενικό πνεύμα, τι κάνει κάποιον Έλληνα, η ελληνική γλώσσα, και ο χρυσός μίτος των δασκάλων.

soul.title_el: Η ψυχή και τα μέρη της
soul.about_en: The soul as the vehicle of nous, holding the body within it, and its three parts.
soul.about_el: Η ψυχή ως όχημα του νου, που κρατά μέσα της το σώμα, και τα τρία μέρη της.

soul.title_el: Ο νους και ο αληθινός εαυτός
soul.about_en: Consciousness as a searchlight, nous, the roles we play and who plays them, and the inner daimon.
soul.about_el: Η συνείδηση ως προβολέας, ο νους, οι ρόλοι που παίζουμε και ποιος τους παίζει, και ο εσωτερικός δαίμων.

soul.about_en: What always is and what always flows, and the soul’s two circles, held at their centre by Hestia.
soul.about_el: Αυτό που πάντα είναι και αυτό που πάντα ρέει, και οι δύο κύκλοι της ψυχής, με κέντρο τους την Εστία.

soul.title_en: The Senses and the Calm Mind
soul.title_el: Οι αισθήσεις και ο γαλήνιος νους
soul.about_en: How sensing reaches the soul, why smell leads to memory, and how practical wisdom and calm arise.
soul.about_el: Πώς η αίσθηση φτάνει ως την ψυχή, γιατί η όσφρηση οδηγεί στη μνήμη, και πώς γεννιούνται η φρόνηση και η γαλήνη.

soul.about_en: The soul’s descent into forgetting, knowing as remembering, truth found by subtraction, and the soul’s many lives.
soul.about_el: Η κάθοδος της ψυχής στη λήθη, η γνώση ως ανάμνηση, η αλήθεια που βρίσκεται με αφαίρεση, και οι πολλές ζωές της ψυχής.

goodlife.about_en: Living well as a relationship with oneself, and eudaimonia as the end the soul carries within, unlike fortune.
goodlife.about_el: Το εὖ ζῆν ως σχέση με τον εαυτό, και η ευδαιμονία ως το τέλος που η ψυχή κουβαλά μέσα της, σε αντίθεση με την τύχη.

goodlife.about_en: Virtue as the soul’s free flow, ethos as habit, healthy shame, the mean, and tending the soul.
goodlife.about_el: Η αρετή ως ελεύθερη ροή της ψυχής, το ήθος ως συνήθεια, η υγιής αισχύνη, το μέτρο, και η καλλιέργεια της ψυχής.

goodlife.about_en: Justice as balance held from the middle, freedom as a present state, and the «No» that needs a «Yes».
goodlife.about_el: Η δικαιοσύνη ως ισορροπία από το κέντρο, η ελευθερία ως παρούσα κατάσταση, και το «Όχι» που χρειάζεται ένα «Ναι».

goodlife.about_en: Paideia as turning the soul, the human as political by nature, and why regimes mirror the soul.
goodlife.about_el: Η παιδεία ως στροφή της ψυχής, ο άνθρωπος ως πολιτικό ον από τη φύση του, και γιατί τα πολιτεύματα καθρεφτίζουν την ψυχή.

eros.about_en: Desire seeking fullness, eros as a current, the heroic path it opens, its two Aphrodites, and peace.
eros.about_el: Η επιθυμία που αναζητά πληρότητα, ο έρωτας ως ρεύμα, ο ηρωικός δρόμος που ανοίγει, οι δύο Αφροδίτες του, και η ειρήνη.

eros.about_en: Diotima the teacher and her ladder of eros, from one beautiful body to the city, then Beauty itself.
eros.about_el: Η Διοτίμα ως δασκάλα και η σκάλα του έρωτα, από ένα ωραίο σώμα ως την πόλη, κι έπειτα ως το ίδιο το κάλλος.

eros.title_el: Η αγάπη που ενώνει τον κόσμο
eros.about_en: Agape as the fullness of union, and philotes, the cosmic love Athena also reads in Poseidon.
eros.about_el: Η αγάπη ως πληρότητα της ένωσης, και η φιλότης, η κοσμική αγάπη που η Αθηνά διαβάζει και στον Ποσειδώνα.

delphi.about_en: Apollo as the god of awakening, the oracle within us, the Delphic E, and his names and powers.
delphi.about_el: Ο Απόλλων ως θεός της αφύπνισης, το μαντείο μέσα μας, το δελφικό Ε, και τα ονόματα και οι δυνάμεις του.

delphi.about_en: Apollo’s first three powers: cleansing and healing, mantic knowing in silence, and a will held on one target.
delphi.about_el: Οι τρεις πρώτες δυνάμεις του Απόλλωνα: κάθαρση και ίαση, μαντική γνώση μέσα στη σιωπή, και θέληση στραμμένη σε έναν στόχο.

delphi.about_en: Apollo’s fourth power: harmonising opposites, returning to the many, and sharing the path in dialogue.
delphi.about_el: Η τέταρτη δύναμη του Απόλλωνα: η εναρμόνιση των αντιθέτων, η επιστροφή στα πολλά, και ο δρόμος που μοιράζεται στον διάλογο.

cave.about_en: The Allegory of the Cave, the prisoners’ double ignorance, conjecture and opinion, and faith as a first step beyond.
cave.about_el: Η αλληγορία του σπηλαίου, η διπλή άγνοια των δεσμωτών, η εικασία και η γνώμη, και η πίστη ως πρώτο βήμα πέρα από αυτές.

cave.title_el: Η ψευδαίσθηση και οι δημιουργοί της
cave.about_en: How interpretation makes illusion, who the wonder-workers are, the new spiritual cave, and watching the mind.
cave.about_el: Πώς η ερμηνεία γεννά την ψευδαίσθηση, ποιοι είναι οι θαυματοποιοί, το νέο πνευματικό σπήλαιο, και η παρατήρηση του νου.

cave.title_el: Η λύση των δεσμών και η στροφή
cave.about_en: The prisoners’ free hands, the sudden release when the soul’s hour is ripe, the turn, and the first light.
cave.about_el: Τα ελεύθερα χέρια των δεσμωτών, η ξαφνική λύση όταν ωριμάσει η ώρα της ψυχής, η στροφή, και το πρώτο φως.

cave.about_en: The Sun simile and the Good beyond it, beholding, and the Divided Line up to participation.
cave.about_el: Η αναλογία του ήλιου και το Αγαθό πέρα από αυτόν, η θέαση, και η διηρημένη γραμμή ως τη μέθεξη.

cosmos.title_el: Ο Ηράκλειτος και το ἀείζωον πῦρ
cosmos.about_en: Heraclitus’ cosmos as ever-living fire, the common Logos, the dry soul, and Aion, the playing child.
cosmos.about_el: Ο κόσμος του Ηρακλείτου ως ἀείζωον πῦρ, ο κοινός Λόγος, η ξηρή ψυχή, και ο Αιών, το παιδί που παίζει.

cosmos.title_el: Το Ένα και η απορροή του
cosmos.about_en: The ineffable One, Plotinus, the outflow from the One down to matter, and science within a unitive worldview.
cosmos.about_el: Το άρρητο Ένα, ο Πλωτίνος, η απορροή από το Ένα ως την ύλη, και η επιστήμη μέσα σε μια ενιαία κοσμοθέαση.

cosmos.title_el: Η μη δυαδικότητα και η υπέρβαση
cosmos.about_en: Seer and seen as one, life as divine play, transcendence, and saying only what the One is not.
cosmos.about_el: Ο θεατής και το θέαμα ως ένα, η ζωή ως θείο παιχνίδι, η υπέρβαση, και το να λες μόνο τι δεν είναι το Ένα.

cosmos.about_en: Pythagoras and union with the Monad, the golden ratio, time as eternity’s image, and the solstice’s dark gate.
cosmos.about_el: Ο Πυθαγόρας και η ένωση με τη Μονάδα, η χρυσή τομή, ο χρόνος ως εικόνα της αιωνιότητας, και η σκοτεινή πύλη του ηλιοστασίου.

mysteries.about_en: Myths as theology in symbols, Homer’s coded laws, the archetype, and three ways to approach a god.
mysteries.about_el: Οι μύθοι ως θεολογία σε σύμβολα, οι κρυμμένοι νόμοι του Ομήρου, το αρχέτυπο, και τρεις τρόποι να προσεγγίσεις έναν θεό.

mysteries.about_en: Zeus as cosmic mind, Dionysus and the Titans, Ares, and the goddess Athena, wisdom ruling force.
mysteries.about_el: Ο Δίας ως κοσμικός νους, ο Διόνυσος και οι Τιτάνες, ο Άρης, και η θεά Αθηνά, η σοφία που κυβερνά τη δύναμη.

mysteries.title_el: Ο θάνατος πριν από τον θάνατο
mysteries.about_en: Philosophy as the practice of dying: not leaving the body, but ceasing to take it for oneself.
mysteries.about_el: Η φιλοσοφία ως μελέτη θανάτου: όχι να εγκαταλείψεις το σώμα, αλλά να πάψεις να ταυτίζεσαι μαζί του.

mysteries.title_en: The Mysteries and the Second Birth
mysteries.title_el: Τα μυστήρια και η δεύτερη γέννηση
mysteries.about_en: Orpheus and the mysteries, Persephone’s descent and return, and the second birth that Christmas still encodes.
mysteries.about_el: Ο Ορφέας και τα μυστήρια, η κάθοδος και η επιστροφή της Περσεφόνης, και η δεύτερη γέννηση που κρύβουν ακόμη τα Χριστούγεννα.

return.about_en: The Odyssey as the soul’s journey home, the suitors still waiting in Ithaca, and insight turned into work.
return.about_el: Η Οδύσσεια ως το ταξίδι της ψυχής προς το σπίτι, οι μνηστήρες που περιμένουν ακόμη στην Ιθάκη, και η γνώση που γίνεται έργο.

return.about_en: A native Greek meditation in three stages, ending in a view with no viewer, and knowing the knower.
return.about_el: Ένας ελληνικός διαλογισμός σε τρία στάδια, που καταλήγει σε θέα χωρίς θεατή, και η γνώση εκείνου που γνωρίζει.

return.about_en: Becoming Nobody, Kazantzakis’ last step, awakening now rather than later, accepting what is, and gratitude.
return.about_el: Να γίνεις Κανένας, το τελευταίο βήμα του Καζαντζάκη, η αφύπνιση τώρα κι όχι αργότερα, η αποδοχή και η ευγνωμοσύνη.

why.truth: Broad and central, so it comes first as what philosophy loves; Athena's reading of it as unforgetting deepens with aletheia in the soul stage.
why.haptesthai: One of Athena's definitions of philosophy's aim, so it belongs with what philosophy is.
why.aporia: Also Apollo's first step (Pythios), but its home is Socrates' not-knowing, which opens the path.
why.maieutics: Socrates' method, met with him; the pregnancy of soul it speaks of is filled out by the second birth.
why.knowthyself: Delphi's command, but the brief and Athena both put it at the start: it is how the path begins. Its deeper reading returns as 'Know the knower'.
why.spirituality: Its label and Athena's view of religion belong at the start; its warrior side comes back with Ares.
why.suffering: Soul group in the data, but Athena reads pain as the soul's alarm clock, so it is part of the call.
why.krisis: Crisis as the fertile ground for change: what sets the journey off.
why.asabove: One of the two principles Athena gives Hellenism; psycho-politics later rests on it.
why.language: Early, because Athena draws teachings out of single Greek words throughout the path.
why.east: Athena's own departure: she went East and was told that what she sought was where she started.
why.goldenthread: A map of the lineage before its teachers are met. Uncertain: it could also sit with Orpheus in the mysteries.
why.daimon: Taught with the soul so that eudaimonia can rest on it; the fire it burns with comes back with Heraclitus.
why.being: Cosmos group, but taught early with the soul because lethe, paideia and the Divided Line all rely on what always is.
why.parmenides: Placed with Being, the one teaching Athena takes from him.
why.becoming: Athena's becoming is the river and sea the soul is plunged into at birth: the open sea of this stage.
why.sameandother: Cosmological in the Timaeus, but for Athena it is the soul's own structure, which the senses rely on.
why.hestia: A goddess, but Athena's Hestia is the still centre of the soul (the Circle of the Same, the hearth that eudaimonia and the mean need), so she is taught with the soul.
why.phronesis: Ethics group, but Athena's φρόνησις is the right motion of the mind through the senses, so it follows them.
why.equanimity: Revealed, not cultivated: the soul's essence that the senses cannot disturb.
why.lethe: Mentions the cave's chains, but the forgetting is the soul's descent, so it is taught here and recalled at the cave.
why.aphairesis: Truth by subtraction follows recollection, and comes before the «No» of the good life, which Athena builds on it.
why.metempsychosis: Part of the soul's journey (Republic X). Uncertain: it could also sit with death in the mysteries.
why.aristotle: Early in the good life because εὖ ζῆν, eudaimonia, telos and entelechy are his.
why.telos: Path group, but it is Aristotle's teleology of eudaimonia, taught with it.
why.entelecheia: Cosmos group, but it is the end the soul carries within, taught with eudaimonia.
why.oikeionergon: From the new Vox talk: the soul's own work, whose fulfilment Athena calls eudaimonia, so it follows entelechy. It touches love and eternity, taught later.
why.measure: The mean as the hearth of virtue; it follows Hestia and the soul's circles.
why.republic: Introduced with justice ('On the Just') so the cave can lean on it later.
why.stoics: Their ataraxia is, for Athena, the core of εὖ ζῆν.
why.noandyes: After truth by subtraction: every subtraction is a «No».
why.courage: After the «No» of 1940 it relies on; its Ares side comes back in the mysteries.
why.paideia: The brief puts it in the good life; the cave, Plato's answer to what paideia is, deepens it later.
why.nature: Cosmos group, but Athena's φύσις here is ethical and political: living κατὰ φύσιν, and de-naturalisation as the twin of depoliticisation.
why.desire: The first rung: behind every desire Athena sees the soul seeking fullness.
why.hero: Path group; Athena derives ἥρως from ἔρως and makes eros the spark of the heroic path, so it follows eros. Uncertain: its labours of self-knowledge could also sit at the call.
why.aphrodite: The brief lists her with the gods, but Athena uses her only for eros' two qualities (Ourania and Pandemos), so she is taught with eros.
why.peace: Two of its three sources are the eros talk (εἰρήνη and ἔρως from one root); its Apollonian side comes back at Delphi.
why.feminine: Follows Diotima, the one woman seen teaching in Plato. Uncertain: it could also sit at the call.
why.politicaleros: The summit of Diotima's ascent in Athena's count, just before Beauty itself.
why.poseidon: A god, but Athena reads him as the higher octave of love, the cohesive force, so he is taught with philotes.
why.will: The archer's passage of Apollo, where the will stops changing.
why.dialectic: Placed as Leschenorios, Apollo's fifth step, which is how Athena frames dialogue.
why.ennead: Closes Delphi: Apollo's nine keys read as 'the new one'.
why.pistis: Plato's πίστις on the Line, which Athena calls the interval between ignorance and knowledge, so it follows conjecture and opinion; its faith in the Good is met later in the stage.
why.freewill: The prisoners' free hands: understood through the cave.
why.horai: Goddesses, but here they are Athena's own gate out of the cave, the soul's ripe hour.
why.spiritualcave: What awakening is not, which needs the cave before it can be named.
why.selfobservation: A practice, but Athena places it where one begins to leave the cave.
why.good: Kept with the Sun simile as the greatest study; earlier stages use εὖ in its plain sense.
why.theasis: The Greek name for awakening, placed where the freed prisoner beholds the Good, as in most of its talks; it deepens with the One.
why.dividedline: Athena reads the Line as the ordering of what the Sun taught, so it follows the Sun and the Good.
why.methexis: The top of the Line; its union with the One is completed in the next stage.
why.drysoul: A Heraclitean fragment, taught with the ever-living fire that dries the soul.
why.aion: Heraclitus' playing child; the Kabeiric Child it also is comes back in the mysteries.
why.matter: Matter as the last outflow of the One, so it follows emanation.
why.kosmotheasis: Path group, but its subject is the unitive worldview against materialism, taught with matter and science.
why.science: Ways group, but taught where its question lives: science within a unitive view of matter and consciousness.
why.proclus: His procession and return frame Athena's two movements; he follows Plotinus as the second Neoplatonist and guides the gods in the next stage.
why.divineplay: Follows Proclus, whose divine sleep it relies on.
why.transcendence: Of Athena's two movements, transcendence needs the One; immanence waits for the return home.
why.apophatic: The brief puts 'what awakening is not' at the call, but this way speaks of the ineffable One, so it follows the One.
why.apeiron: The infinite we are, localised in Hestia's point; it needs the One and non-duality.
why.goldenratio: Built on the Divided Line and on harmony, both taught before.
why.eternity: Time as eternity's moving image, before the solstices.
why.darkness: The solstice's longest night as a gate; the second birth in the mysteries builds on it.
why.homer: Placed with myth: Athena's Homer is the coder of cosmic laws in story. His Odyssey is read at the return.
why.divine: Three ways to approach a god, taught before the gods themselves.
why.herkos: Ares' epithet, after Ares and Hestia.
why.athenagoddess: With Ares, whom she overpowers. Uncertain: she is also Odysseus' guide and could open the return.
why.goldenverses: A Pythagorean text, placed with death because Athena reads its last lines on leaving the body.
why.immortality: The hero's immortality is a state reached by dis-identifying, so it follows death and its practice.
why.orpheus: Founder of the mysteries in Athena's account, so he opens them.
why.hermes: The guide of souls who brings Persephone back, so he follows her.
why.christianity: Thinkers group, but Athena reads Christmas as the latest coding of the second birth, so it follows it.
why.immanence: The second movement: Odysseus who, after Ithaca, must still face the suitors.
why.ergon: 'Make music, and work': after Delphi's music, insight becomes a way of life.
why.knowtheknower: Athena's deepest reading of 'Know thyself', so it comes back near the end.
why.enlightenment: Athena's test of completion is Odysseus' 'Nobody', so it comes after the Odyssey.
why.kazantzakis: His 'even the One does not exist' is, for Athena, the last step to the Source. Uncertain: she cites him across many talks.
why.nyn: Also a teaching on time, but its point is to awaken now, not later: living it now.
why.gratitude: Athena ends her lessons with gratitude, so the path ends with it.
